scope: Aircraft attack temporary speed policy and exact native handback
finding: Attack stage limitSpeed writes had no saved native baseline getter, and cleanup reset to a generic twice-config maximum. speedLimitApplied proved a write but could not preserve a mission cap or a later native limit change.
implementation: Attack no longer writes limitSpeed. Its independent mission value remains untouched.
Native forceSpeed/getForcedSpeed provide an observable temporary cap in metres/second; planned km/h divides by3.6.
First actual write captures original pilot/value. Nonnegative original cap bounds every stage; subsequent stages retain that original baseline.

Pilot/native-cap replacement preempts the old attack. Same-group pilot replacement may restore the unchanged vehicle-policy cap under the original live flight lease. Authored-route resumption also requires that lease; a successor flight controller receives no route recall.

sources.supports: Setter uses km/h and documented reset is default; no saved native limit getter documented.
Native speed limit uses metres/second and negative restores default.
Native paired getter used by existing ground-controller receipt design; flight-specific physical behaviour remains unverified.

validation.initialFinding: One existing source extraction stopped at a nested block terminator; changed its boundary to the following top-level gate, retaining pilot/task guards and adding native cap checks.

remaining: forceSpeed flight response and interaction with independent mission limitSpeed require normal/HC physical validation.
Identical-value external writes are indistinguishable. Missing receipts, changed group/lease and owner migration do not authorize guessed restoration.

flightRelocationCheckpoint.initialFullFinding: Two authored-route source assertions still named the removed limitSpeed writer and old resume gate. Existing assertions updated to actual forceSpeed writer and stronger ownsFlight guard; no tests removed/added.
